Which side of the road do they drive on? Mostly the right. But the red 'left' countries on this map tell a story about empires, trade and one very strange Sunday in Sweden.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ By Wikipedia's count, 141 of the 195 UN-recognised countries drive on the right and 54 on the left. Left-hand traffic still covers roughly a third of the world's people and a quarter of its roads.
2/ Many left-driving countries were British colonies: Australia, New Zealand, India, South Africa. But Japan, Thailand and Indonesia were never British, so empire is not the whole story.
3/ A popular tale says Napoleon spread right-hand driving across Europe. Scholars have found no documentary evidence for it.
4/ Sweden drove on the left until 05:00 on 3 September 1967, 'Dagen H' (H for högertrafik). A 1955 referendum had 83% of voters against switching, but parliament approved it in 1963 anyway.
5/ Only 157 minor accidents were reported on the day. Accident rates were back at their old level by 1969. Iceland made the same switch on 26 May 1968.
6/ It can go the other way too. Samoa moved from right to left on 7 September 2009, so residents could import cheaper used cars from Australia, New Zealand and Japan.
Which of these surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
